chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub and Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Kuleyb ibn Muawiya Al-Asady, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, a servant may become a believer in the morning and an unbeliever in the evening, or an unbeliever in the morning and a believer in the evening; and a people are lent faith (Iman), then it is taken away from them, and they are named 'the lent ones' (Al-Mu'arun); then he (peace be upon him) said: 'So-and-so was from them.'

key_terms.مُعَارِينَ: The Lent Ones (those temporarily granted faith)
key_terms.يُسْلَبُونَهُ: It is taken away from them

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when a person is described as having 'lent faith' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of *Iman al-Mu'ar* (temporary faith), illustrating the fluidity of spiritual states where a believer may become a disbeliever and vice versa. It highlights those 'lent' faith who are subsequently stripped of it, a phenomenon often linked to the instability of those whose faith is superficial or conditional. This serves as a warning against complacency, emphasizing that true faith requires steadfastness rather than transient emotional or circumstantial adherence.
